This report is in response to a resolution by City Council during budget deliberations to examine specific proposals in the Calgary Save and Edmonton reimagined services programs to determine if there is anything that the City of Saskatoon can learn and implement from these initiatives.

As outlined in the report, the City of Saskatoon began its own continuous improvement journey in 2005. This program focused on the use of innovative and creative means to support workplace efficiencies and provide the best possible services to residents.

Cronico these efforts Saskatoon started formally producing the annual service savings and sustainability report in 2014, which has identified more than 400 million in reduced expenditures, deferred cost, time savings and additional revenues.

In recent years, Calgary and Edmonton have embarked on their own efficiency and service level reviews. The two attachments of the report include a comprehensive overview of the initiatives Calgary and Edmonton have directed their respective administrations to proceed with.

This report is requesting approval of the terms of reference for the continuous assurance project.
In accordance with the 2022 approved audit plan, the city internal auditor's office has developed the terms of reference for the continuous assurance project.
This audit will analyze large volumes of data using technology to evaluate controls for key business processes,
which includes but is not limited to procurement,
P cards, vendor payments, corporate revenue, employee payroll, human resources and information technology.
At the initial level, historical data will be analyzed to detect any errors over payments, non-compliances or fraud threats.
However, as a project matures, data will be analyzed on an ongoing basis.
It will provide greater assurance on the whole population and closer to the occurrence of transactions.
Thus, any errors or fraud risk will be detected earlier and at times before the money leaves the city.
I would like to highlight some key control tests, specifically related to employee payroll, procurement and payments.
For employee payroll examples of key control tests would include two or more employees with the same bank account number.
Payments may to employees after the termination date, large vacation balances of employees and unapproved time sheets.
These control tests would detect any duplicate or fictitious employees in the system, inaccurate employee payments, errors and non-compliance with payroll policies and procedures.
For procurement and payments examples of control tests would include vendor employee bank account match, vendor with PO box address,
two or more payments with the same amount purchase orders created after receipt of invoice, purchases made outside of delicate authority
and two or more vendors with the same name bank account or address.
These control tests would detect any fictitious vendors, conflict of interest, fraud risk, duplicate or inaccurate vendor payments, non-compliance,
unauthorized purchases, errors and legal risks.
A list of key criteria that will be used to evaluate controls have been included in the report.
Any outliers or red flags identified as a result of running the data analytics will be investigated in coordination with the respective business areas,
and a root cause analysis will be conducted.
A continuous assurance report will be submitted to the Standing Policy Committee on Finance on a Sami annual basis starting in Q3 of 2022.
The detailed term of reference has been attached in the appendix.
